visual_research.visual_brief: Study real product patterns from the references below. No pre-made colors or fonts are supplied — derive tokens from approved brand direction only.

top_3_products.name: Coursera
top_3_products.what_to_study: Social proof placement: partner logos, learner counts, and outcome stats. Note how they sequence trust before CTA.

top_3_products.name: 80,000 Hours
top_3_products.what_to_study: Editorial narrative flow: long-form sections with article-like rhythm, evidence-first copy, and zero equal-card grids.

top_3_products.name: Kajabi
top_3_products.what_to_study: Instructor authority pattern: named expert photo, short bio line, and course cards that lead with the instructor, not the price.

top_3_inspo_sites.name: Harvard Online (online.harvard.edu)
top_3_inspo_sites.what_to_study: Institutional credibility without decoration: clean typography, proof by affiliation, asymmetric feature blocks.

top_3_inspo_sites.name: Outlier.org
top_3_inspo_sites.what_to_study: Minimalist academic feel: generous whitespace, serif-weight headlines for authority, outcome proof in two lines, no hero image required.

top_3_inspo_sites.name: Luma.id
top_3_inspo_sites.what_to_study: Event/cohort page rhythm: date prominence, speaker credibility, scarcity-aware CTA copy ('Registration closes…').

do_this: vary hero structure per page purpose: home uses proof-first, course detail uses evidence-led split, admin uses compact table-first
lead with a named expert or real cohort photo — no anonymous stock classroom images
keep admin screens compact and scannable: tight row height, status chips, inline actions
sequence trust before CTA: show proof (alumni, partners, outcomes) before asking for registration
use Arabic-first copy in public pages; admin stays LTR
not_this: do not start every section with a centered h2 + three equal cards — break this pattern at least 3 times per page
do not use fake round numbers: '500+ students', '99% satisfaction', '24/7 support' — use real or omit
do not use anonymous stock photos of people smiling at laptops
do not use premade category color palettes — derive all colors from approved brand signals
do not use premade category font pairings — use only approved project fonts
do not repeat the same section structure on adjacent sections of the same page
